why: A buyer signal is a business voice AND work software could remove. These four
are the shapes that actually appear: toil with a number on it, software that
does not exist yet, a tool outgrown, and a terse answer that only makes sense
inside its thread. All synthetic - example.invalid throughout, nothing collected.

record.title: We run a small parts distributor and re-key every order by hand
record.text: Two of us spend about six hours a week copying order details out of emails into a spreadsheet and then into the invoicing tool. We tried to automate it and it breaks whenever a supplier changes their format. Is it worth paying someone to build this properly?

cases.why: No manual-work language at all. Found by a control test: 'we need someone to build X' is as clear a buyer as exists, and work_pain missed it until needs_built was added.

record.title: Our customers keep asking for a portal and we cannot build it
record.text: I own a small manufacturing business. We need someone to build a simple order portal that talks to our ERP. No idea whether to hire a developer or outsource it.

cases.why: Already pays for automation and has outgrown it - the clearest 'now it needs an engineer' moment there is.

record.title: Hit the ceiling of our automation tool
record.text: I run a small agency and we have about forty scenarios stitched together. It costs us a few hundred per month and half of them break when a webhook changes. Do we pay someone to rewrite this properly or keep patching?

cases.why: The measured case. Alone this is three words with no ownership language; under a survey post it is a business owner naming work they would pay to remove. Ambiguous on purpose: an inherited voice is weaker evidence than a stated one.

record.text: chasing late invoices, every single month

context.title: What is one part of running your small business you wish you could automate?
